description.summary: bento's private connection to its shell

protocol.description:
The shell is the program bento's config names with `shell`. bento starts it and hands it a connection of its own through WAYLAND_SOCKET; this global is only on that connection.
Through it, the shell gets the commands and events meant for the shell, and asks bento for glass behind its surfaces.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Glass objects made from it stay valid.

request.name: get_glass
request.description:
Makes the glass object for a layer surface. The surface has no glass until the object gets shapes. Only layer surfaces show glass; it's ignored on other surfaces.
A surface can have one glass object at a time.

entry.name: glass_exists
entry.summary: the surface already has a glass object

event.name: style
event.description: Sent once bound and whenever the config changes it. The shell's own surfaces line up with the windows by these: the gaps between windows and their corner radius, in logical pixels.

event.name: toggle_launcher
event.description: Sent when the toggle-launcher action runs, like from a shortcut.

interface.name: bento_glass_v1
interface.description:
bento draws glass behind the surface in the shapes it's given: it refracts and blurs what's behind them and lights their edges. Shapes that come close melt into one piece of glass, so a surface can grow one shape out of another.
The surface draws its own tint over the glass.

request.name: destroy
request.description: The glass goes away on the surface's next commit.

request.name: set_shapes
request.description:
The shapes, as an array of int32 quintuples: x, y, width, height and corner radius, in the surface's logical coordinates. An empty array removes the glass.
Double-buffered: it applies on the surface's next commit.

entry.name: invalid_shapes
entry.summary: the array isn't whole quintuples, has more than 8 shapes, or a shape has a negative size or radius
